lantern-copper-921

The documents describe **Strata**, a local AI serving system that runs the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model on a single NVIDIA or AMD GPU plus system RAM, exposing an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API at `127.0.0.1:8080`. The `AI_SETUP.md` page is written for AI coding agents installing Strata on a user's PC: it mandates keeping the server loopback-only unless paired with an API key, flags model download sizes (~70–111 GB), RAM-based model selection (IQ1_M through UD-Q4_K_XL), and resumable long-running setup. Hardware requirements include RTX 20/30/40/50 or listed Radeon cards with ≥12 GB VRAM, 32 GB+ RAM, and ~80 GB disk; older CPUs fall back to an experimental slow build.

`AMD_HIP.md` details the HIP backend supporting gfx1100 (RX 7900), gfx1101 (7800 XT), gfx1200/gfx1201 (RDNA4: RX 9060/9070 XT, AI PRO R9700), gfx1030 (RDNA2), and an opt-in gfx906 wave64 build for MI50/MI60/Radeon VII. It maps CUDA-shaped runtime calls to HIP/hipBLAS, uses RDNA2/3/4 signed integer dot instructions, supplies wave32 shuffles, and offers calibrated hipBLASLt tuning tables per architecture/version. ROCm installs via TheRock wheels into `.venv` (~10 GB, no sudo); Windows uses a prebuilt engine zip with bundled ROCm libraries since 0.1.34, addressing DLL shadowing, stale errors, WDDM budgeting, and PCIe event timing quirks. Multi-GPU layer splits and `"split_skip_if_fits"` are documented, with measured RDNA4 speeds (e.g., R9700 4K prefill ~982 tok/s, decode ~45 tok/s), WMMA opt-ins, router fast-path, and community-validated card reports.
